title: Inodes
definition: Index Node. A data structure on a Linux file system that stores all the metadata about a file (permissions, owner, size, physical location on the disk), except for the file's actual name and data.
simpleExplanation: The library index card. The file's name is just a pointer to the index card. The index card (inode) tells the computer exactly which physical magnetic sectors on the hard drive contain the data.
realWorldExample: You run `df -i`. It shows 100% Inode usage, even though `df -h` shows the hard drive is only 10% full. A bug created millions of tiny 1-byte files. You ran out of 'index cards' before you ran out of hard drive space. The server crashes.

basic: Does an inode contain the name of the file?
intermediate: When you `mv` (rename) a file in Linux, does its inode number change?

answers.question: Contains the name?
answers.answer: No. The filename is stored in the Directory file. The Directory simply maps the human-readable name to the hidden inode number.

answers.question: Does inode change on rename?
answers.answer: No. The inode remains exactly the same. Linux simply updates the Directory file to point a new name at the same inode, which is why renaming a 100GB file is instant.
